text:
Philip Broberg is playing like the defenseman Edmonton drafted eighth overall in 2019, and he's doing it in St. Louis. He has 19 points in 26 games, 8 of them goals, after 34 points all of last season. He's up to 25 minutes a night and on the ice for 54% of the Blues' power-play time, nearly double last season's share. He scored again in the win over Dallas on Friday, his fourth goal in six games.

Here's the catch. Those 8 goals came on 4.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he's shooting 14% after 6% last season. The Blues have also scored 13.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice, which inflates the assists. At five on five, St. Louis takes only 47% of the expected goals with him out there. The finishing will likely cool.

The skill underneath is real, though. He hit the fastest skating speed in our data (100th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 95th percentile in chances from the home-plate area last season. The role is earned; the pace is borrowed.
